subject: history
title: Roots of the Vietnam War Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll trace Vietnam from French colony to the 1954 partition.
meta_desc: GCSE History — French Indochina, Dien Bien Phu and Geneva 1954.
final_note: You learned how French defeat split Vietnam at the 17th parallel.

Eisenhower fear that Asia would fall to communism

walkthroughs.body_html:
France ruled Indochina from 1887, growing rubber and rice.

Ho Chi Minh founded the Indochinese Communist Party in 1930 and led the Viet Minh from 1941. He declared independence on 2 September 1945 — but France returned to crush it.

From 1946 the First Indochina War dragged on. The US paid 80% of French costs.

At Dien Bien Phu in 1954 General Giap's troops surrounded the French. France surrendered after 56 days — losing 11,000 prisoners.

The 1954 Geneva Accords split Vietnam at the 17th parallel.

Ho's communists held the North; Ngo Dinh Diem ran the Catholic South. Elections were due in 1956 but Diem refused. Eisenhower warned of falling dominoes if the South collapsed.

mcqs.q: What were the Wars of the Roses really about?
options: The Truman Doctrine ordered the dropping of the atomic bomb on Japan.
The whole country was at war for thirty continuous years.
They were a religious war between Catholics and Protestants.
Dynastic conflict between rival branches of the Plantagenets (Lancaster and York) over the throne, intensified by weak kingship under Henry VI and noble factionalism.

mcqs.q: Why did the League of Nations fail to prevent WWII?
options: The League failed because no countries joined it.
The League failed because Hitler banned it in 1933.
Absence of the US, requirement of unanimous decisions, no armed force of its own, weak responses to Manchuria (1931) and Abyssinia (1935), and great-power self-interest.
The Truman Doctrine ordered the dropping of the atomic bomb on Japan.

mcqs.q: What did the Truman Doctrine commit the US to in 1947?
options: The League failed because Hitler banned it in 1933.
Supporting free peoples resisting communist takeover — initially Greece and Turkey — formalising the policy of containment articulated by George Kennan.
The Truman Doctrine declared war on the Soviet Union.
The Truman Doctrine ordered the dropping of the atomic bomb on Japan.
